newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin stable, stays on in hospital.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin stable, stays on in hospital.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, recovering in hospital from pneumonia, is in a stable condition and his temperature is normal, Kremlin spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky said on Monday.

"In the doctors' opinion, the president is in a stable condition. His temperature and other indicators are in the normal range," Yastrzhembsky told a Kremlin briefing after doctors examined the president.

Asked to comment on reports that 65-year-old Yeltsin might leave Moscow's Central Clinical Hospital on Tuesday or Wednesday, Yastrzhembsky said: "I have no confirmation that the president will be released tomorrow or the day after."
He said the Kremlin press service would announce news about Yeltsin's release from hospital as soon as it had any information.
Top Kremlin doctor Sergei Mironov said on Friday that Yeltsin would probably spend another three days in hospital before moving to a country residence for three weeks of convalescence.
Yeltsin, who was taken to hospital last Wednesday, was visited by members of his family on Sunday.
Yeltsin had a quintuple heart bypass operation on November 5 and returned to work in the Kremlin on December 23. Doctors have said his latest illness is not related to his heart problems.
